title: Fixed-shape injections pass a phase test for nine TESS CPV schedules at offsets up to 0.1%
abstract: We test whether cadence gaps and folding-period errors can cause apparent phase changes in complex periodic variables (CPVs). We retrieve 18 public TESS SPOC light-curve files for one rejected pair from each of nine stars in an earlier harmonic phase test. Two templates per pair repeat without change at the actual cadence times. We test nine period offsets, eight initial phases, median division and two folding choices. All 4,032 branch trials at offsets up to 0.1% from the geometric mean of the released periods pass the test. All are informative. At +0.3%, two fixed-shape cases fail with the released folding periods, both with and without median division. None of 2,592 true-period control trials fails. In total, 4 of 5,184 branch trials fail and 257 are uninformative. The results strengthen the phase test against the tested small errors and give a processing counterexample at a larger error. They do not fit the observed later curves or measure material survival. Selected failures, a sparse deterministic grid, no injected noise, fixed estimated templates and no period search limit inference. Code, aggregate results, input hashes and separate-scratch regeneration steps are included.

display.caption: Fixed-shape test rejection by injected period offset. Each point contains 144 cases. The same two cases at +0.3% fail before and after median division. No trial fails at offsets up to 0.1%.
